chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces one non-existent instruction ("release its phase") with another claim that this diff never establishes: the new reason says `` `ddflow unblock <phase id>` releases a whole phase``. The bug report this change is supposed to fix states that `ddflow unblock` "takes exactly one item id (usage: ddflow unblock [--note] id) and there is no phase-level release anywhere in `ddflow --help`." The diff touches only the reason string and a test; it adds no phase-level release and provides no evidence that passing a phase id to `unblock` cascades to release the held children. Given the reported environment (`archive_globs` matching `docs/todo.md`, task `159.A.1` held with reason "in an archive file"), an agent that follows the new advice and runs `ddflow unblock 159.A` will, if `unblock` acts on the single id it is given, leave `159.A.1` still held — the exact failure the bug describes, just reworded. The fix is only correct if `unblock <phase>` is actually recursive, which nothing in the change shows or tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The change only rewrites the hold string; it adds no phase-level release anywhere in the command layer. Yet the new text — ``ddflow unblock <phase id>` releases a whole phase`` — advertises exactly that capability, and the bug report this change claims to fix explicitly states that `ddflow unblock` takes a single item id and that "there is no phase-level release anywhere in `ddflow --help`". So the fix replaces one unactionable instruction ("release its phase") with another instruction whose validity the change never establishes: nothing in the diff makes `unblock <phase id>` cascade to a phase's held tasks. The only new test does not actually check that following the advice works — it asserts `run_cli(repo, "unblock", "159.A")[0] == OK` and never inspects the state of `159.A.1`, the item that carries the reason. Given input `docs/todo.md` in `archive_globs` with a held task `159.A.1` whose hold is recorded per item at import, a command that flips only the phase item (or returns OK without recursing into children) would satisfy the test while leaving `159.A.1` held, i.e. the reported 791 held tasks would still not be driveable by the advice printed in their reason. To guard the fix, the test needs to assert that `159.A.1` (and the subtree) actually leaves HOLD after the call, not merely that the invocation exits 0.

The bug this change closes was explicitly premised on the opposite — that `ddflow unblock` takes exactly one item id, that there is no phase-level release anywhere in `ddflow --help`, and that the only way to act on the hold is per-task `unblock` calls. The diff touches only this string and one test; it adds no phase-targeting code path. The only support offered for the new claim is `run_cli(repo, "unblock", "159.A")[0] == OK`, i.e. a zero exit status, which is satisfied both by a real subtree release and by a no-op/success-on-non-held-id path. The previous finding on this line still holds because the diff did not answer it (no phase-level release was added) and the new test does not probe cascade behavior.

The comment `# the advice works as written` is not backed by the assertion beneath it. The test checks only that the CLI exited `OK`; it never re-reads state to confirm `_state(repo).items["159.A.1"].state == OPEN` or that `159.A.1.blocked_reason` cleared. Given input where `unblock 159.A` returns success without releasing the held child — e.g. because `159.A` is a section node that is not itself held, or the phase id is accepted and ignored — this test passes while the hold on `159.A.1` remains, which is precisely the failure mode the bug is about. The earlier finding on this test also still holds: the triage is `untriaged` and the only assertion on the "advice works" path is still an exit-code check.

chunk_findings.detail: The prior finding is not answered by this diff. The change touches only the human-readable reason string plus a test: nothing in `ddflow/services/importer.py`, and nothing anywhere in the command layer, adds a phase-level release. The new text advertises ``ddflow unblock <phase id>` releases a whole phase``, and the only new evidence offered is `assert run_cli(repo, "unblock", "159.A")[0] == OK`. That assertion checks only the process exit code; it never re-reads the state to confirm that `159.A.1`'s own `blocked_reason` was cleared or that the item became drivable. Concretely: the hold is recorded per item on `159.A.1` (the test itself reads `_state(repo).items["159.A.1"].blocked_reason`), so if `unblock 159.A` merely resolves/marks the phase node and does not cascade to descendants, the test still passes green while every held task keeps its "in an archive file (...)" reason — exactly the 791-distinct-phase situation the bug report describes. Since the diff supplies no command-layer implementation and no verification that following the advice clears the held item, the advertised capability remains unproven (and, on the evidence in the bug report that `ddflow unblock` takes exactly one item id with no phase release in `ddflow --help`, still false). To close this, either implement the phase release in the command layer or change the message to the operation that is actually verified to clear the item's hold, and make the regression test assert on the resulting item state rather than the exit code.
